justifications.c1: UK pest-infestation prosecutions carry £12k–£20k penalties (Pearl Food Distribution £16,400, Express & Star, search-confirmed; Barking wholesaler £15k+; Poundland £134k retail), but none names an open door as the cause and no recall cost was found, so the £ link to door dwell time is indirect.
justifications.c2: Doors and pest prevention (4.4.8) are a recurring BRCGS non-conformity with 'doors left open' a typical finding (LRQA datasheet, search-confirmed), but that is per annual audit; no data on how often or how long dock doors stand open, and no required routine check.
justifications.c3: Pest contractors record open doors as conducive conditions, sites use rapid-closing doors and screens, and Technical Managers manage pest visits, but no time or £ cost of the current door-policing routine was found.
justifications.c4: BRCGS Issue 9 clause 4.4.8 says external doors to open product areas shall not be opened during production except in emergencies, with pest precautions where opened (SafetyCulture templates and IFSQN, search-confirmed), and doors are a frequent audit non-conformity (LRQA); no rule requires door-open time to be measured or logged.
justifications.c5: Technical Manager adverts (Reed £42k–£52k, DWP, DR Newitt) name pest-control management among duties, so the job title owning the risk is evidenced; budget size and ownership of the pest contract are not.
justifications.c6: Pest contractors visit audited food sites and already sell connected monitoring (Rentokil PestConnect claims 9,000+ devices across 268 food sites, vendor; Anticimex SMART by subscription) and record open doors on service reports; no door module in their offers was found.
justifications.c7: Door-open sensors are a commodity (consumer alarm £13.49, LoRaWAN contacts $60–£69, Monnit ~$94–$115, dock alarms $190); the only gap (linking door time to the pest programme) is evidenced by absence, and no one is shown paying for door-dwell data.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf LoRaWAN magnetic door contacts at £55–£69 (Milesight EM300-MCS, Linovision, Multi-Tech) and a pre-certified LTE-M module are evidenced, so a sub-£50 BOM is plausible; whether fire-door fittings need approval is an open question.
justifications.c9: BRCGS re-audits each cycle with door findings recurring, and pest monitoring is sold by subscription (Anticimex, myRentokil, unpriced), but there is no record-keeping duty for door data and no evidence anyone pays a recurring fee for it.
justifications.c10: Certification-body audit data (LRQA), council and trade-press prosecutions (Enfield, Food Manufacture) and first-hand IFSQN forum threads on open doors (titles only); the prosecutions do not tie infestations to doors.

weakest: Door-open sensing is a commodity, and nothing shows a food site paying for door-dwell data or any infestation cost traced to an open door.
